title: Stacked Recurrent Neural Machine Translation Architecture
description: This diagram shows a multi-layer encoder-decoder model where blue blocks represent the source encoding phase and red blocks represent the target decoding phase. The hidden states flow horizontally through time and vertically through layers, with the <eos> token signaling the transition from input sequence A-B-C-D to output sequence X-Y-Z.
teaches: A learner sees how a stacked recurrent neural network architecture processes a source sequence through an encoder and then generates a target sequence word-by-word through a decoder.
benchmark_query: diagram of a stacked two-layer rnn encoder-decoder showing source sequence A B C D and target sequence X Y Z with eos token
source_title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation

title: Global Attention Mechanism in Seq2Seq Models
description: An encoder-decoder structure where all encoder hidden states are weighted by global alignment weights to produce a context vector. This context vector is then combined with the current target state to predict the next output.
teaches: A learner sees how a global attention mechanism aggregates source hidden states into a single context vector to assist in generating a target state.
benchmark_query: diagram of global attention layer calculating context vector from all source states and global align weights for target state prediction
source_title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation

title: Local Attention Mechanism in Neural Machine Translation
description: The diagram illustrates an encoder-decoder sequence where an attention layer identifies an aligned position to focus on a window of source states. These states are weighted to form a context vector that informs the generation of the current target word.
teaches: A learner sees how a local attention mechanism selects a window of source hidden states to compute a context vector for a specific target position.
benchmark_query: diagram showing local attention layer with context vector and aligned position window over source hidden states for target word generation
source_title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation

title: Residual Learning Building Block Architecture
description: An input x passes through two weight layers and a ReLU activation while a parallel shortcut carries the identity x to be added to the output. This combined sum F(x) + x then undergoes a final ReLU activation.
teaches: A learner sees how a residual block bypasses weight layers with an identity connection to perform an additive operation before the final activation.
benchmark_query: diagram of a residual building block showing x identity shortcut bypass weight layers and addition to F(x) followed by relu
source_title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

title: Standard and Bottleneck Residual Blocks
description: The left diagram shows a standard residual block with two 3x3 convolutions, while the right diagram illustrates a bottleneck design that uses 1x1 convolutions to compress and then expand the feature map dimensions.
teaches: A learner sees how a standard residual building block compares to a bottleneck residual block using 1x1 convolutions to reduce and then restore dimensionality.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing standard residual block with 3x3 layers to a bottleneck block with 1x1 64, 3x3 64, and 1x1 256 layers
source_title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
description: An RL algorithm takes actions in an environment and receives observations, while a reward predictor processes those observations and human feedback to provide a reward signal.
teaches: A learner sees the relationship between an RL agent, an environment, and a reward predictor that incorporates human feedback.
benchmark_query: diagram showing rl algorithm receiving predicted reward from a reward predictor module fed by human feedback and environment observations
source_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences

title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention Architecture
description: The process begins with matrix multiplication of Q and K, followed by scaling and an optional mask. Finally, a SoftMax operation is applied before a final matrix multiplication with V to produce the output.
teaches: A learner sees the computational flow of scaled dot-product attention, starting from Query, Key, and Value inputs through matrix multiplication, scaling, masking, and softmax operations.
benchmark_query: diagram of scaled dot-product attention showing flow from Q K and V through MatMul Scale Mask and Softmax layers

title: Transformer Attention Visualizing Anaphora Resolution
description: The diagram displays words from a sentence in two parallel columns representing self-attention links. Bold lines connect the word 'its' in the top layer to 'Law' and 'application' in the bottom layer, showing how the model focuses on relevant context to resolve pronouns.
teaches: A learner sees how a self-attention head in a Transformer model resolves anaphora by linking the pronoun 'its' to the nouns 'Law' and 'application'.
benchmark_query: visualization of self-attention head layer 5 resolving the pronoun 'its' to 'Law' and 'application' in a transformer model

title: Comparison of Deep Learning Normalization Methods
description: Four cubes represent feature map tensors with axes for Batch (N), Channels (C), and Spatial dimensions (H, W). Blue regions highlight which pixels are grouped together to compute normalization statistics for Batch Norm, Layer Norm, Instance Norm, and Group Norm.
teaches: A learner sees how different normalization techniques group feature map pixels across batch, channel, and spatial dimensions to calculate mean and variance.
benchmark_query: visualize dimensions used for mean and variance in batch norm layer norm instance norm and group norm with N C H W axes

title: World Model Architecture for Reinforcement Learning
description: The system processes observations through a Vision Model (V) to produce latent vectors (z), which are integrated by a Memory RNN (M) to track history (h). A Controller (C) then combines the current latent state and memory to select an action (a).
teaches: A learner sees how a world model architecture integrates vision, memory, and a controller to map environment observations to actions over time.
benchmark_query: diagram of a world model with vision model V encoding z, memory RNN M tracking state h, and controller C choosing action a

title: World Model Agent Architecture
description: Visual observations are compressed into latent vectors by a VAE, which are then passed to an MDN-RNN and a controller. The controller combines current latent states and hidden memory to produce actions that influence the environment.
teaches: A learner sees how a world model agent uses a VAE for vision, an MDN-RNN for memory, and a controller to interact with an environment.
benchmark_query: diagram of world model agent with VAE (V) MDN-RNN (M) and controller (C) showing feedback loop between environment and actions

title: BERT Input Representation Construction
description: Tokens from two sentences are combined with special symbols like [CLS] and [SEP]. The final input is the element-wise sum of its specific token embedding, a segment embedding (A or B), and a position embedding.
teaches: A learner sees how BERT constructs input representations by summing token, segment, and position embeddings for a given sequence of text.
benchmark_query: diagram showing the summation of token embeddings E[CLS], segment embeddings EA/EB, and position embeddings E0-E10 for BERT input representations
source_title: BERT : Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: BERT vs GPT vs ELMo Architectures
description: This diagram compares the data flow of three NLP models, showing how embeddings (E) pass through Transformer (Trm) or LSTM layers to produce output tokens (T). BERT uses bidirectional attention, GPT uses left-to-right attention, and ELMo uses a concatenation of separate forward and backward LSTMs.
teaches: A learner sees the structural differences in how BERT, OpenAI GPT, and ELMo process context, specifically comparing bidirectional, unidirectional, and concatenated unidirectional architectures.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing bidirectional transformer connections in BERT vs left-to-right transformer in GPT and concatenated LSTMs in ELMo using E and T labels
source_title: BERT : Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: Fine-tuning BERT on Different NLP Tasks
description: The diagram illustrates how BERT uses special [CLS] and [SEP] tokens to handle tasks ranging from sentence classification to token-level tagging and question answering. It shows the mapping from input embeddings through transformer layers to specific task outputs like class labels or start/end spans.
teaches: A learner sees how a pre-trained BERT model is adapted for different downstream tasks like sentence pair classification, single sentence classification, question answering, and named entity recognition by modifying input tokens and output layer heads.
benchmark_query: how bert handles different tasks using [CLS] and [SEP] tokens for sequence classification versus token-level tagging in question answering SQuAD and NER
source_title: BERT : Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: T5 Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer Framework
description: The diagram shows a central T5 model processing various task-specific input strings on the left to produce corresponding target text outputs on the right. Examples include translating English to German, sentiment classification, and document summarization using natural language prefixes.
teaches: A learner sees how diverse NLP tasks like translation, classification, and summarization are unified into a single text-to-text format for a model like T5.
benchmark_query: diagram showing T5 model mapping translate English to German input to Das ist gut output and cola sentence to not acceptable label
source_title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

title: T5 Span Corruption Unsupervised Objective
description: Original text is modified by replacing consecutive corrupted words with unique sentinel tokens like <X> and <Y>. The model is then trained to predict these missing spans as targets delimited by the same tokens.
teaches: A learner sees how a span-corruption unsupervised objective transforms original text into input sequences with sentinel tokens and corresponding target output spans.
benchmark_query: T5 span corruption diagram showing original text inputs and targets with <X> and <Y> sentinel tokens for masked spans
source_title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

title: Attention Mask Patterns in Transformer Architectures
description: Matrices illustrate three attention masks where dark cells indicate allowed attention from output index y to input index x. The causal mask forms a lower triangular pattern, while the prefix mask allows full attention for early tokens before transitioning to a causal structure.
teaches: A learner sees how different attention mask patterns (fully-visible, causal, and causal with prefix) restrict which input tokens can be attended to at each output timestep.
benchmark_query: Compare fully-visible, causal, and causal with prefix attention mask matrices for self-attention with input x and output y labels.
source_title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

title: Dreamer Reinforcement Learning Workflow
description: The process flows from a dataset of experience to learned latent dynamics where observations are encoded into states, and finally to a phase where value and actions are learned via latent imagination.
teaches: A learner sees how a reinforcement learning agent transitions from a dataset of experience to learning world dynamics and finally optimizing behavior through imagination in a latent space.
benchmark_query: three stage diagram showing dataset of experience, learned latent dynamics with encoders, and value and action learned by latent imagination with trophy icon
source_title: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination

title: World Model Dynamics with Latent Imagination
description: An encoder maps observations (o) to latent states (green circles), which then predict rewards (r) and reconstruct observations (ô) while transitioning based on actions (a). This recurrent structure allows an agent to model temporal dynamics and anticipate future outcomes.
teaches: A learner sees how a world model processes observations into latent states to predict future rewards and reconstruct environment frames across time steps.
benchmark_query: diagram of world model dynamics showing encoder and decoder mapping between observation o and latent states with reward r and action a predictions
source_title: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination

title: Latent Imagination in Reinforcement Learning
description: An encoder maps an observation into a latent state, from which the model recurrently predicts future states, rewards, values, and actions. Icons for trophies, coins, and joysticks represent value, reward, and action predictions respectively across a sequence of imagined steps.
teaches: A learner sees how a latent state space model predicts future rewards, values, and actions sequentially from an initial observation and subsequent imagined transitions.
benchmark_query: diagram of latent state space model predicting v_hat r_hat and a_hat sequences from observation o_1 using imagination
source_title: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination

title: Language Model Meta-Learning and In-Context Learning
description: The diagram illustrates the hierarchical relationship between SGD-based pre-training as an outer loop and rapid task adaptation within an input sequence as an inner loop. Example sequences demonstrate patterns like addition, word unscrambling, and translation that the model learns to continue based on provided context.
teaches: A learner sees how large-scale unsupervised pre-training (the outer loop) enables in-context learning (the inner loop) where a model adapts to specific sub-tasks like arithmetic or translation within a single forward pass.
benchmark_query: diagram showing learning via SGD during unsupervised pre-training as outer loop and in-context learning as inner loop for sequence patterns

title: In-context learning vs traditional fine-tuning
description: The diagram contrasts three in-context learning methods where examples are included in the prompt against fine-tuning which uses gradient updates for each training example. It illustrates the prompt structure for zero, one, and few-shot settings using an English-to-French translation task.
teaches: A learner sees how zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot in-context learning differ from traditional fine-tuning by varying the number of task examples provided in the prompt without performing weight updates.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing zero-shot one-shot and few-shot prompt engineering with traditional fine-tuning gradient updates for language models

title: Vision Transformer ViT Architecture
description: The architecture shows an input image divided into patches which are then linearly projected and combined with position embeddings before entering a transformer encoder block. The encoder consists of multi-head attention and MLP layers with residual connections and layer normalization, leading to a classification head.
teaches: A learner sees how an image is tokenized into patches, embedded with positional information, and processed through a transformer encoder for classification.
benchmark_query: diagram of vision transformer architecture showing linear projection of flattened patches position embeddings and transformer encoder layers with multi-head attention
source_title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

title: CLIP Contrastive Pre-training and Zero-Shot Prediction
description: Text and image encoders generate embedding vectors that are compared in a similarity matrix to align matching pairs. These learned encoders then allow for zero-shot classification by comparing an image embedding against embeddings of several candidate text labels.
teaches: A learner sees how contrastive pre-training aligns image and text embeddings in a shared space to enable zero-shot classification via natural language prompts.
benchmark_query: contrastive pre-training diagram showing I and T embedding matrix with zero-shot prediction from label text prompt a photo of a {object}
source_title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

title: Perceiver Model Architecture and Data Flow
description: The architecture maps a large input byte array to a smaller latent array using cross-attention, followed by a series of transformer blocks and optional iterative cross-attention steps. This allows the model to process high-dimensional inputs with a constant computational complexity in the latent space.
teaches: A learner sees how a Perceiver model uses a fixed-size latent bottleneck to iteratively attend to a high-dimensional input byte array via cross-attention and latent transformer blocks.
benchmark_query: perceiver architecture diagram showing cross attention between latent array N x D and byte array M x C with iterative repeats
source_title: Perceiver: General Perception with Iterative Attention

title: Swin Transformer vs Vision Transformer Hierarchies
description: The Swin Transformer creates multi-scale feature maps (4x, 8x, 16x) by merging local windows, supporting dense tasks like segmentation. In contrast, the standard ViT maintains a single 16x resolution across all layers, primarily suited for classification.
teaches: A learner sees how a Swin Transformer builds a hierarchical representation by merging patches across layers, unlike the standard Vision Transformer (ViT) which maintains a constant resolution.
benchmark_query: comparison of hierarchical feature maps in swin transformer vs single low resolution feature maps in ViT for classification and segmentation
source_title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows

title: Shifted Window Partitioning in Swin Transformers
description: Layer l uses a regular grid of windows for self-attention, while Layer l+1 shifts these windows to bridge the previous boundaries. Individual patches are grouped into local windows, and the shift ensures information flows between adjacent regions.
teaches: A learner sees how shifting window partitions between layers enables cross-window connections in a transformer architecture.
benchmark_query: how shifted window partitioning in layer l and l+1 creates connections between previous window boundaries in swin transformer architecture
source_title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows

title: Decision Transformer Architecture for Reinforcement Learning
description: States, actions, and target returns are interleaved as tokens in a causal transformer sequence. The model uses self-attention over past timesteps to predict the next action needed to achieve the target return.
teaches: A learner sees how reinforcement learning can be framed as a sequence modeling task where returns, states, and actions are tokens processed by a causal transformer to predict future actions.
benchmark_query: Architecture diagram of a causal transformer processing interleaved return-to-go R_t, state s_t, and action a_t tokens to predict action a_t.
source_title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling

title: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) Architecture
description: An input vector x is passed simultaneously through frozen pretrained weights W and a pair of low-rank matrices A and B. The outputs are summed to produce the final hidden representation h.
teaches: A learner sees how a Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) module runs in parallel with frozen pretrained weights, using a low-rank decomposition to modify the output of a neural network layer.
benchmark_query: diagram showing pretrained weights W summed with low rank matrices A and B where A is initialized with Gaussian distribution and B is zero
source_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

title: Masked Autoencoder (MAE) Architecture
description: An image is divided into patches, most of which are masked out before the encoder processes the remaining visible patches. The decoder then takes the encoder outputs combined with mask tokens to reconstruct the full target image.
teaches: A learner sees how a Masked Autoencoder (MAE) processes an image by encoding only visible patches and using a decoder to reconstruct the original image from encoded patches and mask tokens.
benchmark_query: diagram of Masked Autoencoder (MAE) architecture showing encoder processing visible patches and decoder using mask tokens to reconstruct full image
source_title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners

title: Perceptual vs Semantic Image Compression
description: The chart plots Distortion (RMSE) against Rate (bits/dim), showing how Autoencoder+GAN models achieve low distortion at higher bitrates while Latent Diffusion Models enable semantic compression at very low bitrates. Image samples at the bottom illustrate the shift from precise reconstruction to semantically similar but pixel-different generations.
teaches: A learner sees the trade-off between rate and distortion in image compression, where perceptual compression reduces pixel-level redundancy and semantic compression focuses on high-level content using generative models.
benchmark_query: rate-distortion curve comparing semantic compression via latent diffusion models and perceptual compression via autoencoder plus GAN with image samples
source_title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

title: Latent Diffusion Model Architecture with Cross-Attention
description: An encoder maps images into a latent space where a diffusion process occurs, while a denoising U-Net utilizes cross-attention to incorporate external conditioning such as text or images. The final denoised latent is then projected back to pixel space using a decoder.
teaches: A learner sees how latent diffusion models integrate conditioning information like text or semantic maps into a denoising U-Net through a cross-attention mechanism within a compressed latent space.
benchmark_query: Architecture diagram of latent diffusion models showing the interaction between the denoising U-Net, cross-attention modules with QKV, and the conditioning encoder tau_theta.
source_title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

title: RLHF Pipeline for Large Language Models
description: This diagram illustrates the reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) process, showing how supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reward model (RM) training, and PPO-based policy optimization work together. It details the flow from prompt sampling and human ranking (D > C > A = B) to iterative policy updates using reward signals.
teaches: A learner sees the three-stage RLHF pipeline: supervised fine-tuning from demonstrations, training a reward model based on human rankings of outputs, and optimizing the final policy using PPO against that reward model.
benchmark_query: three step process for training language models to follow instructions using human ranking feedback reward model and proximal policy optimization PPO
source_title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

title: Reflexion Agent Architecture with Verbal Reinforcement
description: An agent architecture where an Actor generates actions based on short-term trajectory and long-term experience, while an Evaluator and Self-reflection module process environment feedback to update memory.
teaches: A learner sees how a language model agent utilizes self-reflection and dual memory systems to improve its actions through environmental feedback.
benchmark_query: Architecture diagram of an agent using Self-reflection (LM) to update Experience (long-term memory) based on Evaluator (LM) feedback from Environment trajectories.
source_title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

title: Generative Agent Memory Architecture
description: An agent perceives input into a memory stream, which then flows through retrieval to inform actions. Internal feedback loops use retrieved memories to generate plans and reflections that are fed back into the memory stream.
teaches: A learner sees the cyclical relationship between perception, memory storage, retrieval, planning, and reflection in an autonomous agent architecture.
benchmark_query: diagram showing generative agent memory stream connecting perceive, act, plan, and reflect modules with retrieval loop
source_title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

title: Comparison of LLM Prompting Paradigms
description: Four diagrams compare standard Input-Output (IO) prompting with Chain of Thought (CoT), Self Consistency (CoT-SC), and Tree of Thoughts (ToT). Each rectangle represents an intermediate 'thought' step, showing how ToT allows for exploring multiple paths and backtracking to find an optimal solution.
teaches: A learner sees the structural evolution of prompting techniques from direct input-output to sequential chains, ensemble voting, and tree-based search with backtracking.
benchmark_query: comparison diagram of IO CoT CoT-SC and Tree of Thoughts ToT illustrating search paths and intermediate thought boxes
source_title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models

title: Comparison of Finetuning Methods and Memory Flow
description: The diagram compares full finetuning, LoRA, and QLoRA, highlighting differences in bit-precision for the base model and optimizer state. It specifically shows QLoRA's use of a 4-bit transformer and paging flow to the CPU to manage memory spikes.
teaches: A learner sees how QLoRA reduces memory requirements compared to Full Finetuning and LoRA by using a 4-bit transformer base, paged optimizers on the CPU, and low-rank adapters.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing full finetuning 32-bit optimizer state vs lora 16-bit adapters vs qlora 4-bit transformer with cpu paging flow
source_title: QLoRA : Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs

title: Multi-Agent Conversation Flow for Secure Code Execution
description: A Commander agent orchestrates a workflow where a Writer agent generates code and logs, while a Safeguard agent provides clearance for security. The process iterates through code generation, safety verification, and execution until a final answer is returned to the user.
teaches: A learner sees how a multi-agent system coordinates between a Commander, a Writer, and a Safeguard to safely generate and execute code in response to user questions.
benchmark_query: Interaction flow between Commander, Writer, and Safeguard agents for secure python code generation and execution in a multi-agent system.
source_title: AutoGen : Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation

title: AutoGen Dynamic Group Chat Workflow
description: The process flows from a manager selecting an agent (Alice, Bob, or User Proxy), asking them for a response, and then broadcasting that response to all other agents in the group.
teaches: A learner sees the three-step cycle of a multi-agent group chat: speaker selection, response generation, and broadcasting the message to other participants.
benchmark_query: three step cycle of select speaker ask speaker to respond and broadcast message in autogen group chat manager
source_title: AutoGen : Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation

title: Multi-agent conversational chess system architecture
description: Two AI/human hybrid players communicate game moves and natural language reasoning to each other while a central Chess Board agent validates rules and maintains state. The diagram shows the flow of move validation requests and the conversational exchange between players using speech bubbles and board states.
teaches: A learner sees how a central multi-agent board manager validates moves and coordinates natural language communication between two autonomous or human-assisted AI chess players.
benchmark_query: diagram of a multi-agent chess system where a board agent validates moves between player agents using natural language and board state
source_title: AutoGen : Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation

title: Single-Path vs Multi-Path Reasoning in LLMs
description: This diagram contrasts single-path reasoning techniques like Chain of Thought (CoT) with multi-path strategies such as Tree of Thoughts (ToT). It illustrates the flow from prompts to LLM outputs, showing how multi-path reasoning explores multiple parallel or branching step sequences to reach a solution.
teaches: A learner sees how large language models can generate reasoning steps through either a single sequential path or various multi-path structures like consistency checks and tree-based searches.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing CoT, ReWOO, CoT-SC, and ToT architectures for single-path and multi-path reasoning in large language models
source_title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents

title: Evolution of the Mamba Block Architecture
description: The diagram illustrates the transition from H3 and Gated MLP to the simplified Mamba block, showing the placement of SSM, convolution, and linear projections. It highlights how the Mamba block integrates a gated branch with a sequence transformation branch using SiLU activations.
teaches: A learner sees how the Mamba architecture is derived by combining and simplifying elements from the H3 block and the Gated MLP.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing H3 block and Gated MLP architecture showing how they combine into the Mamba block with SSM and Conv layers
source_title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

title: Convolutional Layer with Fully Connected Output
description: A sequence of input nodes X0 through X8 are processed in overlapping pairs by shared weights A, which then all connect to a single output layer F.
teaches: A learner sees how a convolutional layer with sliding windows feeds into a fully-connected layer in a neural network.
benchmark_query: diagram showing 1D convolution with shared weights A applied to inputs X followed by a fully connected layer F
source_title: Conv Nets: A Modular Perspective - colah's blog

title: Sliding Window Architecture in Convolutional Neural Networks
description: A 2D grid of input nodes labeled X maps to a grid of processing units labeled A, which then all converge into a single output unit F. This illustrates how local features are extracted across an image and then aggregated.
teaches: A learner sees how a convolutional layer applies a shared function 'A' across a grid of local input patches to produce a feature map that feeds into a subsequent global operation 'F'.
benchmark_query: diagram showing grid of input X_i,j nodes connecting to shared processing units A and aggregating into a single top node F in a CNN
source_title: Conv Nets: A Modular Perspective - colah's blog

title: MLP Network in Network Layer Decomposition
description: The diagram illustrates the 'Network in Network' concept where a single processing block is expanded into a mini neural network. It shows two input ports connecting to a hidden layer of nodes n0-n2, which feed into n3-n4, finally converging to a single output.
teaches: A learner sees how a single abstract layer 'A' in a neural network can be decomposed into a multi-layer perceptron with internal nodes n0 through n4.
benchmark_query: diagram showing a green block A expanded into a sub-network with nodes n0 n1 n2 feeding into n3 n4
source_title: Conv Nets: A Modular Perspective - colah's blog

title: Visualizing Convolution through Sequential Probability Distributions
description: Two sequential random drops follow probability distributions f(a) and g(b). The final position is the sum of the distances a and b, illustrating the fundamental mechanic of convolving two functions.
teaches: A learner sees how the composition of two independent probability distributions results in a total distance sum represented by the convolution of the individual density functions.
benchmark_query: diagram showing two normal distributions stacked with distances a and b summing to a plus b for convolution explanation

title: Edge Detection via Pixel Differentiation Kernel
description: A 5x5 kernel matrix with adjacent -1 and 1 values is shown next to its effect on an image of the Taj Mahal. This operation highlights vertical edges where neighboring pixel values differ significantly.
teaches: A learner sees how a small convolution kernel with -1 and 1 values acts as an edge detector by highlighting pixel intensity differences.
benchmark_query: 5x5 image kernel with -1 and 1 adjacent cells applied to Taj Mahal for vertical edge detection

title: Weight Sharing in 1D Convolutional Neural Networks
description: The diagram shows a series of identical neurons A processing an input sequence x to produce an output y. Each neuron shares the same weights w0 and w1, applied to overlapping sliding windows of the input vector.
teaches: A learner sees how a 1D convolutional layer applies the same weights and neuron structure across different positions of an input sequence.
benchmark_query: diagram of a 1D convolutional layer showing weight sharing with labels w0 and w1 connecting inputs x to neurons A

title: Basic Computational Graph with Value Evaluation
description: Nodes represent variables and operations while arrows indicate the flow of data. Input values for variables a and b propagate through addition and multiplication nodes to calculate a final result e.
teaches: A learner sees how a mathematical expression is decomposed into a computational graph where nodes represent intermediate variables and directed edges show dependencies.
benchmark_query: computational graph showing nodes c = a + b and d = b + 1 leading to e = c * d with numerical values a=2 b=1

title: Computational Graph with Local Derivatives
description: Nodes represent mathematical operations like addition and multiplication with specific values, while arrows show the dependency flow labeled with local partial derivatives.
teaches: A learner sees how local partial derivatives are assigned to the edges of a computational graph during a forward pass to enable gradient calculations.
benchmark_query: computational graph showing nodes e=c*d and c=a+b with local partial derivatives de/dc and dc/da labeled on edges

title: Forward-Mode Differentiation Path Accumulation
description: The diagram illustrates a sequence of nodes where the derivative of the input with respect to itself is 1. Moving forward, the derivative of Y is the sum of path weights alpha, beta, and gamma, which is then multiplied by the sum of weights delta, epsilon, and zeta to find the derivative of Z.
teaches: A learner sees how forward-mode differentiation accumulates derivatives by summing path weights from an input node through intermediate nodes to an output node.
benchmark_query: forward-mode differentiation diagram showing partial derivatives dX/dX=1 and dZ/dX as (alpha+beta+gamma)(delta+epsilon+zeta) in a graph

title: Reverse-Mode Differentiation Path Accumulation
description: Nodes represent variables and their partial derivatives with respect to the output Z, while arrows represent the local influence of one variable on another. Moving from right to left, the process sums local contributions at each node and multiplies them by the accumulated gradient to propagate derivatives back to the input.
teaches: A learner sees how reverse-mode differentiation (backpropagation) aggregates local gradients along multiple paths by summing them at nodes and multiplying them as it moves backwards.
benchmark_query: diagram of reverse-mode differentiation showing partial derivatives dZ/dX and dZ/dY using greek letters alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta to represent paths

title: Reverse-Mode Differentiation on a Computational Graph
description: The diagram shows a directed graph where nodes contain partial derivatives of the final output 'e' and edges represent local derivatives between adjacent nodes. The value of de/db is calculated by summing the paths through intermediate nodes c and d.
teaches: A learner sees how reverse-mode differentiation (backpropagation) calculates the gradient of a final output with respect to all intermediate and input nodes in a computational graph.
benchmark_query: reverse-mode differentiation graph showing partial derivative de/db = 5 using paths through nodes c and d with local gradients

title: Unrolling a Recurrent Neural Network
description: A single module A with a feedback loop is shown as equivalent to a chain of multiple copies of A. Each step takes an input x and produces an output h while passing information to the next time step.
teaches: A learner sees how a recurrent neural network loop is equivalent to an unrolled sequence of identical modules processing sequential inputs.
benchmark_query: diagram showing the equivalence of a looped recurrent neural network module A and its unrolled form with inputs x0 x1 x2 and outputs h0 h1 h2

title: RNN Short-Term Dependency
description: An unrolled recurrent neural network shows input tokens x0 through x4 passing through hidden states A to produce outputs h0 through h4. Blue glows indicate that the output h3 is primarily derived from the recent inputs x0 and x1.

benchmark_query: Venn diagram showing intersection of off-policy data, function approximation, and bootstrapping with DQN at the center representing the deadly triad.

title: Deep Q-Learning Architecture and Data Flow
description: The diagram illustrates transitions from an environment being stored in a replay buffer, sampled in minibatches to train an online Q-network using Huber loss, while a separate frozen target network provides stable regression targets and periodically copies weights from the online network.
teaches: A learner sees how a Deep Q-Network (DQN) manages data flow between an environment, a replay buffer, and two separate networks (online and target) to stabilize training.
benchmark_query: DQN architecture diagram showing replay buffer D, online Qw network, frozen target Qw- network, and Huber loss gradient path.

title: Breaking Feedback Loops with Target Networks
description: The diagram illustrates a feedback loop where weight updates for current states also increase the targets for next states. A frozen copy of the weights is used to 'cut the edge' and stabilize learning by providing a static target.
teaches: A learner sees how training on a single network can lead to unstable feedback loops in Q-learning and how a frozen target network breaks this cycle.
benchmark_query: how a frozen copy of weights Qw- cuts the edge to prevent the next target y = 1 + gamma max Qw from rising indefinitely

title: Search and Distillation Loop in RL
description: A four-step cycle shows a model being refit on transitions, then used to label states via search, which in turn trains an actor network before collecting new real-world data. Mathematical symbols like f_phi for the model and pi_theta for the actor policy clarify the mapping between components.
teaches: A learner sees the cyclic process of search and distillation in model-based reinforcement learning, where model fitting, state labeling, policy regression, and data collection interact.
benchmark_query: diagram of cyclic process refitting model f_phi, labeling states with search seeded by pi_theta, and regressing actor onto labels (si, ai*)

title: Branched Rollouts vs Long Imagined Rollouts
description: The chart compares real state trajectories with short orange branched rollouts and a single long gray rollout, illustrating how prediction error compounds over time. While the long rollout drifts significantly from real data, resetting to real states in the replay buffer keeps the model's 'imagined' transitions more accurate.
teaches: A learner sees how short branched rollouts from real data states limit the accumulation of model error compared to one long continuous trajectory.
benchmark_query: schematic showing how short 3 step branched rollouts from real states in a replay buffer minimize compounding error compared to long rollouts

title: On-Policy vs Off-Policy vs Offline Reinforcement Learning
description: Three side-by-side diagrams illustrate how policies interact with environments and replay buffers. On-policy uses fresh batches, off-policy maintains a buffer of multiple previous policies, and offline learning uses a fixed dataset without environment interaction.
teaches: A learner sees the differences in data flow and environment interaction between on-policy, off-policy, and offline reinforcement learning paradigms.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing on-policy off-policy and offline RL data flows including policy update expectations and fixed dataset D collected once

title: Stitching in Offline Reinforcement Learning
description: Two sub-optimal paths on a grid intersect at cell 10. By performing a per-transition backup, the learner combines the beginning of one episode with the successful ending of another to form a new complete route to the goal.
teaches: A learner sees how offline reinforcement learning can 'stitch' parts of different sub-optimal episodes together to discover a successful path to a goal that was never seen as a single complete sequence.
benchmark_query: stitching on the frozen lake reinforcement learning diagram showing blue episode ending in hole 11 and orange reaching goal through cell 10

title: Parameter Space versus Policy Space Updates
description: A sigmoid function maps parameters theta to action probabilities, showing that a delta theta of 2 causes a large policy shift near the origin but negligible change in saturated regions. The side-by-side bar chart visualizes these probability distributions before and after the updates.
teaches: A learner sees how fixed-size parameter updates result in drastically different policy changes depending on the gradient of the mapping function, illustrating the difference between parameter space and policy space.
benchmark_query: visualize how the same delta theta update of 2 leads to delta pi of 0.38 versus 0.002 depending on sigmoid slope sigma prime
source_title: Trust Regions and Proximal Policy Optimization

title: Clipping vs Squashing in Action Selection
description: Panel (a) compares a clip function with zero-slope regions to a tanh function with positive slope everywhere for gradient-based optimization. Panel (b) illustrates how clipping a Gaussian distribution results in a point mass at the boundary, whereas squashing maps the density across the entire bounded interval.
teaches: A learner sees how squashing functions like tanh maintain non-zero gradients across a range compared to clipping, and how they distribute probability density versus creating a point mass.
benchmark_query: comparison of gradient slopes and probability density distributions for 2tanh(u) squashing versus hard clipping in bounded action spaces

title: Score Function as Gradient of Log-Density
description: The left plots show a 1D bimodal density where the score is zero at modes and valleys, while the right plot shows a 2D score field with arrows pointing toward high-density regions.
teaches: A learner sees how the score function, defined as the gradient of the log-density, points towards the modes of a probability distribution in both one and two dimensions.
benchmark_query: Relationship between probability density p(x) and its score function d/dx log p(x) in 1D and 2D vector fields pointing to modes.

title: Effect of Gaussian Blur on Data Modes
description: Four panels show a 2D probability density with three modes marked by crosses. As the noise parameter sigma increases from 0 to 2, the separate clusters merge until the individual modes are no longer distinguishable.
teaches: A learner sees how increasing Gaussian noise standard deviation sigma blurs distinct data modes into a single distribution.
benchmark_query: visualizing how increasing sigma in gaussian noise blurs three distinct data modes into a single bump in a 2D density plot

title: Distribution Matching Distillation Training Loop
description: Noise is mapped to a sample by a one-step student model, which is then perturbed with noise to time t. The gradient for the student is calculated as the difference between the scores provided by a frozen teacher and a second model trained on the student's samples.
teaches: A learner sees how distribution matching distillation uses a frozen teacher and an auxiliary student-trained model to compute gradients for a single-step generator.
benchmark_query: diagram of distribution matching distillation showing gradient for theta as (grad log q_theta,t - grad log p_t) transpose dx_t / dtheta

title: Forward and Reverse Diffusion Process Chain
description: The diagram illustrates a sequence of states from data x0 to noise xT. Blue arrows represent the fixed forward Gaussian transitions, while orange arrows represent the learned reverse Gaussian transitions for generation.
teaches: A learner sees how a diffusion model transitions from data to noise through a fixed forward Markov chain and reconstructs it via a learned reverse process.
benchmark_query: diagram showing forward process q(xk|xk-1) and reverse process p_theta(xk-1|xk) Gaussian chains from data x0 to noise xT
source_title: Gaussian Paths: Diffusion and Flow Matching

title: U-Net Architecture with Time and Label Embeddings
description: An encoder-decoder structure uses skip connections to concatenate high-resolution features. A conditioning block at the bottom shows how time and class label embeddings are summed and added to every processing block.
teaches: A learner sees how a U-Net architecture processes input images through down-sampling blocks, a bottleneck, and up-sampling blocks with skip connections, while integrating time and label embeddings.
benchmark_query: U-Net diagram showing 28x28x1 input with two down-sampling stages to 7x7x128 bottleneck and time t sinusoidal feature embedding addition.

title: Latent Diffusion Model Architecture
description: An encoder compresses input x into a lower-dimensional latent z0, where diffusion (adding and removing noise) occurs, before a decoder maps the result back to image space x-hat. Numerical examples show the massive reduction in data dimensions for both MNIST-style and Stable Diffusion-scale inputs.
teaches: A learner sees how latent diffusion models use an encoder to map high-resolution images into a smaller latent space where noise is added and removed, before a decoder reconstructs the final image.
benchmark_query: diagram showing encoder mapping image x to latent z0 with noise z1 added for training and removed for sampling with dimension labels

title: Three Conditioning Mechanisms for GANs
description: The diagram illustrates concatenation of noise and embeddings, feature modulation via scale and shift operations, and a projection discriminator head combining feature maps with class embeddings.
teaches: A learner sees three distinct architectural patterns for incorporating conditional information into neural networks: concatenation, feature modulation, and projection heads.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing concatenation G([z; ec]), modulation a(c)h + b(c), and projection head D(x, c) = ecT phi(x) + psi0(x) architectures

title: DCGAN Generator and Critic Architecture
description: The generator transforms a 1x1x100 latent vector into a 64x64x3 image using transposed convolutions, while the critic mirrors this by downsampling the image to a single logit via strided convolutions. Both paths detail layer dimensions, normalization steps, and activation functions like ReLU and Leaky ReLU.
teaches: A learner sees how a DCGAN generator and critic (discriminator) map data between a 100D latent vector and a 64x64 image using transposed and strided convolutions.
benchmark_query: DCGAN architecture diagram showing generator and critic layers from 1x1x100 latent z to 64x64x3 image including batch normalization and activation functions.

title: Checkerboard Artifacts in Transposed Convolutions
description: The left panel shows a 3x3 kernel with stride 2 creating uneven overlap counts (4, 2, 1), while the right panel shows a 4x4 kernel with stride 2 creating a uniform overlap count of 4.
teaches: A learner sees how the choice of kernel size relative to stride in a transposed convolution affects the overlap count of output pixels, potentially causing checkerboard artifacts.
benchmark_query: visualize overlap counts of 3x3 kernel versus 4x4 kernel with stride 2 in transposed convolutions to explain checkerboard artifacts

title: Generative Adversarial Network Training Process
description: The generator G transforms latent noise z into generated samples G(z), while the critic D learns to assign high scores to real data and low scores to generated data. Optimization involves a feedback loop where the generator's updates are driven by gradients flowing back through the critic's realness logits.
teaches: A learner sees how a Generative Adversarial Network alternates between updating a discriminator to score real vs. generated data and updating a generator through the discriminator's gradient.
benchmark_query: diagram of GAN training showing generator G mapping latent draw z to generated batch G(z) and critic D outputting realness logits

title: Jensen-Shannon Divergence Saturation and Vanishing Gradients
description: This plot shows JS(p, q) between two normal distributions as a function of the mean shift mu. The divergence curve flattens completely at approximately 0.693 (log 2), illustrating why GAN training can fail when distributions are too far apart.
teaches: A learner sees how the Jensen-Shannon divergence between two Gaussians saturates at log 2 as their mean shift increases, leading to vanishing gradients.
benchmark_query: plot of Jensen-Shannon divergence JS(p, q) saturation at log 2 for normal distributions with mean shift mu

title: Comparison of JS, Wasserstein, and MMD Gradients
description: Three panels compare the gradients produced by Jensen-Shannon divergence, Wasserstein distance (W1), and Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) between two non-overlapping distributions p and q. JS results in zero slope, while W1 provides a constant unit slope and MMD provides a smooth gradient directed toward the target distribution.
teaches: A learner sees how different divergence measures (JS, Wasserstein, and MMD) provide different gradients when two probability distributions have non-overlapping supports.
benchmark_query: visualize gradients of JS divergence vs Wasserstein W1 vs MMD kernel witness for disjoint distributions p and q

title: Shift Invariance in Single-Sample vs Pairwise Scoring
description: Two plots compare a single-sample critic score D(x) against a zero threshold with a pairwise difference D(x) - D(x'). It demonstrates that adding a constant bias 'b' changes whether a sample is classified as real or generated, but does not change the distance or order between two samples.
teaches: A learner sees how shifting critic scores by a constant value affects single-sample classification relative to zero but leaves the relative ranking and differences between pairs invariant.
benchmark_query: diagram showing how adding a constant b to critic score D(x) changes single-sample thresholding but leaves pairwise difference D(x) - D(x') unchanged

title: Sequential Synchronous and Asynchronous Trial Scheduling
description: The diagram compares three scheduling methods across a timeline: sequential processing on one worker, synchronous parallel processing with idling gaps due to stragglers, and asynchronous parallel processing where workers start new trials immediately.
teaches: A learner sees how sequential, synchronous, and asynchronous trial scheduling impacts total execution time and worker utilization.
benchmark_query: Comparison of sequential synchronous and asynchronous scheduling showing trial idle time and stragglers on a time axis

title: Synchronous Successive Halving Scheduling
description: The diagram illustrates two workers processing multiple trials across different rungs. It highlights the idle time on Worker-1 during Rung 0 caused by the need to wait for Worker-0's Trial-2 to complete before moving to Rung 1.
teaches: A learner sees how synchronous successive halving forces worker nodes to wait for the slowest trial in a rung before proceeding to the next level of evaluation.
benchmark_query: diagram showing synchronous successive halving with worker-0 and worker-1 idle time waiting for trial-2 to finish rung 0

title: Asynchronous Successive Halving Algorithm Execution
description: Two worker timelines show trials being executed and promoted to higher rungs. Promotions occur immediately when enough information is available, allowing for continuous resource utilization without idle time.
teaches: A learner sees how two workers asynchronously execute hyperparameter trials and promote successful ones to higher rungs without waiting for a synchronous global barrier.
benchmark_query: Asynchronous successive halving diagram showing Worker-0 and Worker-1 timelines with trial promotions to Rung 1 and Rung 2.

title: Two-Stage Wake-Word and Assistant Model Pipeline
description: An audio signal enters a small 10^5 parameter wake-word model on a phone; if it detects the wake-word, it activates a 10^11 parameter assistant model in a data center to process the actual request.
teaches: A learner sees how a two-stage speech recognition system uses a small on-device wake-word model to trigger a much larger, cloud-based assistant model.
benchmark_query: diagram showing wake-word model on phone with 10^5 parameters vs assistant model in data center with 10^11 parameters for speech processing

title: LLM Pretraining and Adaptation Pipeline
description: Unlabeled web text is used for next-token prediction to create a base model. This model is then branched into a classifier, assistant, or agent via fine-tuning, preference learning, or tool integration.
teaches: A learner sees how a large-scale unlabeled dataset is used for self-supervised pretraining to create a base model, which is then specialized into different functional outputs through various adaptation techniques.
benchmark_query: diagram showing pretraining on web text next token prediction leading to base model then fine-tuning for classifier assistant and agent

title: Reinforcement Learning Feedback Loop
description: An agent sends an action to the environment, which responds by returning an observation of the new state and a reward signal back to the agent.
teaches: A learner sees how an agent and an environment interact through a cycle of actions, observations, and rewards.
benchmark_query: diagram showing the feedback loop between agent and environment with action reward and observation boxes and directional arrows

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
description: A log-log plot showing training loss against compute for four model sizes ranging from 10^8 to 10^11 parameters. Each model curve eventually plateaus, while a dashed line represents the Pareto frontier of the best possible model for any given compute budget.
teaches: A learner sees how larger models achieve lower loss but require more compute, forming an optimal scaling frontier shown by a power-law envelope.
benchmark_query: log-log plot of loss vs training compute showing the envelope of best models for parameter counts from 10^8 to 10^11

title: Three Types of Machine Learning Distribution Shift
description: Comparison of covariate shift, label shift, and concept shift across source and target data distributions. Each panel shows class probability distributions (y=0, y=1) for a 1D input x and the resulting optimal decision boundary.
teaches: A learner sees how covariate, label, and concept shifts affect data distributions and decision boundaries between source and target domains.
benchmark_query: visual comparison of covariate shift vs label shift vs concept shift showing changes in p(y|x) and p(x|y) distributions and decision boundaries

title: Geographic Concept Shift in Language
description: A choropleth map of the US uses a ternary color scale to represent the prevalence of the terms 'pop', 'soda', and 'coke' by county. It illustrates how the meaning or label associated with a concept changes based on geographic context.
teaches: A learner sees how regional variations in language (dialectal shifts) across the United States manifest as geographic distributions of the terms pop, soda, and coke.
benchmark_query: ternary color scale map of United States counties showing the distribution of the terms pop soda and coke for concept shift examples

title: Feedback Loop in Predictive Policing
description: A cycle shows how model predictions for crime in area A lead to more patrols, which results in more recorded crimes, which then biases the training data to reinforce the original prediction.
teaches: A learner sees how biased model predictions create a self-reinforcing feedback loop in predictive policing through data logging and retraining.
benchmark_query: diagram showing feedback loop between model predicts more crime in A and training data hold more crime in A via logging and retraining

title: VC Dimension and Shattering Points in 2D
description: Eight panels on the left show every possible binary labeling for three points, all separable by a line. The two panels on the right show configurations of four points (XOR pattern and interior point) that cannot be linearly separated.
teaches: A learner sees how a linear classifier can shatter three non-collinear points by achieving all possible labelings, whereas it fails to shatter certain four-point configurations.
benchmark_query: diagram showing linear separator shattering 3 non-collinear points with all 8 labelings and failing to shatter 4 points in R2

title: Logits usage in training versus evaluation
description: The diagram contrasts the differentiable path using softmax and cross-entropy for optimization with the discrete path using argmax for calculating classification accuracy. It shows a logit vector for 'cat', 'chicken', and 'dog' resulting in a loss value of 0.37 and a 'correct' accuracy label.
teaches: A learner sees how the same logit vector is processed through softmax for training loss and argmax for evaluation accuracy.
benchmark_query: diagram showing logits vector flowing into softmax for smooth cross-entropy loss versus argmax for discrete accuracy calculation

title: Cross-Entropy Loss vs Zero-One Error Rate
description: The chart compares a discrete step function representing classification error with a smooth blue curve representing cross-entropy loss. It shows that as the margin m becomes negative, indicating a wrong prediction, both the error and the loss increase.
teaches: A learner sees how cross-entropy loss acts as a smooth, continuous surrogate for the non-differentiable zero-one classification error as a function of the margin m.
benchmark_query: plot showing cross-entropy loss log2(1 + e^-m) as a convex upper bound to zero-one classification error versus margin m

title: Effect of temperature on softmax probability distributions
description: Three bar charts compare softmax outputs for classes 'cat', 'chicken', and 'dog' at temperatures of 0.25, 1.0, and 4.0. Low temperature sharpens the prediction toward the highest logit, while high temperature flattens the distribution across all classes.
teaches: A learner sees how varying the temperature parameter T in a softmax function transforms a set of logits into different probability distributions, ranging from nearly one-hot to nearly uniform.
benchmark_query: bar charts showing softmax(o/T) for classes cat chicken dog at T=0.25 sharper T=1 softmax and T=4 flatter

title: Bias-variance tradeoff and model complexity
description: The chart plots error against model complexity, showing test error as a U-shaped curve with a minimum at the best complexity level. It identifies the generalization gap as the difference between increasing test error and decreasing training error during overfitting.
teaches: A learner sees how training error and test error evolve relative to model complexity, defining regions of underfitting and overfitting.
benchmark_query: plot of training error vs test error showing noise level and generalization gap during overfitting

title: K-Fold Cross-Validation Process
description: The dataset is divided into K equal-sized folds. In each of the K rounds, one unique fold is used for validation while the rest are used for training, finally averaging all validation scores.
teaches: A learner sees how a dataset is partitioned into five folds for cross-validation, with a different fold serving as the validation set in each of the five training rounds.
benchmark_query: diagram of 5-fold cross-validation showing validation fold moving across rounds 1 to 5 and averaging the K validation scores

title: Minibatch Stochastic Gradient Descent Training Loop
description: A four-stage cycle shows data flowing through a forward pass to compute predictions, calculating a mean squared error loss, performing automatic differentiation for gradients, and updating weights and bias terms.
teaches: A learner sees the four iterative steps of minibatch stochastic gradient descent: the forward pass for predictions, loss calculation, backward pass for gradients, and parameter updates.
benchmark_query: diagram of four step training loop showing forward pass y=Xw+b, loss calculation, backward pass gradients, and weight update w-eta*grad_L

title: Matrix Vector Representation of Linear Regression
description: This diagram illustrates the equation y-hat = Xw + b, showing how a weight vector w multiplies each row of feature matrix X to produce predictions, while the scalar bias b is added to every entry through broadcasting.
teaches: A learner sees how matrix dimensions align in a linear regression model, specifically how weights are applied to features and how a scalar bias is broadcast across multiple training examples.
benchmark_query: diagram of y-hat = Xw + b showing matrix dimensions n x d for features and d for weights with scalar bias broadcasting

title: Linear Regression and Residuals
description: Blue points represent observed data y(i), while the black line represents predictions y-hat(i). Vertical blue bars illustrate the residuals or errors between the actual values and the regression line.
teaches: A learner sees how linear regression fits a line to data points by measuring the vertical distance between observed values and the predicted regression line.
benchmark_query: diagram showing vertical residuals between data points y(i) and a linear regression line y-hat(i) on an x-y coordinate plane

title: Least Squares as Orthogonal Projection
description: The vector y is projected onto a plane representing the column space of X, resulting in the prediction vector y-hat. The residual vector r is shown as a perpendicular line connecting y to the plane, illustrating the minimum distance solution.
teaches: A learner sees how the least squares solution is an orthogonal projection of the target vector onto the column space of the feature matrix.
benchmark_query: geometric interpretation of least squares as orthogonal projection of y onto the column space of X with residual vector r

title: Gradient Descent vs Minibatch SGD Convergence Paths
description: Two plots compare smooth gradient descent paths (black) against noisy minibatch SGD paths (colored) on a loss surface. Reducing the learning rate eta from 0.2 to 0.05 results in a smaller 'noise ball' of fluctuations around the global minimum.
teaches: A learner sees how the learning rate and batch size affect the convergence path and noise levels of stochastic gradient descent compared to full-batch gradient descent.
benchmark_query: comparison of gradient descent and minibatch SGD paths on loss contours with different learning rates eta 0.2 and 0.05 showing noise balls

title: Probabilistic Interpretation of Linear Regression
description: The regression line y = wx + b represents the mean of a normal distribution p(y|x) at every point x, with data points scattered according to this Gaussian noise model.
teaches: A learner sees how linear regression assumes that target values are sampled from a normal distribution centered on the regression line for any given input.
benchmark_query: diagram showing normal distribution p(y|x) centered on regression line wx+b for probabilistic linear regression model

title: Regression Loss Functions and Noise Models
description: Two panels compare probability density functions of noise models with their associated penalty curves. The left plot shows Gaussian and Laplace distributions with a log-scale inset for tail comparison, while the right plot displays squared, absolute, and Huber loss functions relative to error.
teaches: A learner sees the mathematical relationship between the shape of noise distributions (Gaussian and Laplace) and their corresponding loss functions (squared error and absolute error), including the Huber loss as a hybrid.
benchmark_query: comparison of Gaussian and Laplace noise densities with squared error, absolute error, and Huber loss penalty functions including log scale tail view

title: Training vs Validation Loss Plotting Alignment
description: The chart illustrates that minibatch losses fluctuate throughout an epoch, leading to a mean training loss plotted at e + 1/2. In contrast, the validation loss is computed using final epoch parameters and is plotted at e + 1.
teaches: A learner sees how training loss is averaged over minibatches and plotted at the midpoint of an epoch, while validation loss is calculated at the end of the epoch.
benchmark_query: explanation of why training loss is plotted at e + 1/2 while validation loss is plotted at e + 1 in machine learning charts

title: Geometry of L1 vs L2 Regularization
description: The diagram compares a circular L2 constraint and a diamond-shaped L1 constraint against elliptical loss contours. It illustrates that the optimal regularized solution w_lambda is likely to land on an axis for L1, setting one parameter to zero.
teaches: A learner sees how L1 regularization (lasso) promotes sparsity by forcing the loss contours to meet the weight constraint at a sharp corner on an axis, unlike L2 regularization (ridge) which meets the smooth circular constraint away from the axes.
benchmark_query: geometric comparison of L1 diamond and L2 circle constraints with elliptical loss contours meeting at axes for sparsity

title: Ridge Shrinkage Factor vs Regularization Constant
description: The plot shows the shrinkage factor mu/(mu + lambda) on the y-axis against lambda on a log scale for several values of the eigenvalue mu. Each curve demonstrates that the shrinkage factor is 0.5 when lambda equals mu and approaches zero as lambda becomes much larger than mu.
teaches: A learner sees how the ridge shrinkage factor varies with the regularization constant lambda across different eigenvalues mu, illustrating that directions with smaller eigenvalues are penalized more heavily.
benchmark_query: plot of ridge shrinkage factor mu/(mu + lambda) vs lambda for different eigenvalue mu 0.01 1 and 100 on log scale

title: RAG Pipeline Stages Metrics and Failure Classes
description: A vertical flow chart showing the stages from query to judge, mapped to specific evaluation metrics like Recall@k and failure types such as 'ranked low' or 'false abstention'. It clarifies the relationship between the retrieval process, the generation quality, and the final evaluation step.
teaches: A learner sees the standard pipeline for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), including how each stage is evaluated and common failure modes like retrieval misses or grounded generation errors.
benchmark_query: RAG pipeline stages with corresponding failure classes like not retrieved ranked low ignored unsupported and metrics like recall@k and cov@T

title: Skip-Gram with Negative Sampling Process
description: The diagram illustrates a sliding window selecting 'steam' as the center word and 'piston' as a context word. It shows how the center word vector and context word vectors are multiplied and compared against noise samples to calculate loss.
teaches: A learner sees how the Skip-Gram with Negative Sampling (SGNS) model selects a positive context pair and samples multiple negative 'noise' words to train word embeddings through inner products.
benchmark_query: diagram of skip-gram with negative sampling showing center vector v_w, context vector u_o, and noise words like 'season' or 'river' with target 0

title: The Lifecycle of an AI Benchmark
description: The chart tracks a benchmark's progress from introduction to replacement, highlighting the gap between public and fresh test sets caused by distribution shifts and the ceiling imposed by label errors.
teaches: A learner sees the four stages of an AI benchmark's lifecycle—introduction, climbing, saturation, and replacement—and how model performance varies across public and fresh test sets due to distribution shifts and overfitting.
benchmark_query: schematic showing benchmark lifecycle stages introduced climbed saturated replaced with curves for public test set vs fresh test set and overfitting gap
source_title: Evaluation Suites, Judges and Error Bars

title: Three Methods for Scoring Language Models
description: The diagram compares Cloze scoring using token log-probabilities, Letter scoring focusing on specific option identifiers, and Generative scoring which involves parsing a model's natural language reply.
teaches: A learner sees three different ways to evaluate a language model on a multiple-choice question: cloze scoring of answer tokens, letter-based log-probability, and generative parsing.
benchmark_query: three scoring conventions for multiple-choice questions comparing log p of full answer text vs letter log p vs generative parsing

title: Forward and Backward Passes on Computational Graphs
description: The top panel shows a forward pass calculating intermediate variables and a final output while recording edge weights. The bottom panel demonstrates the backward pass, where adjoints are propagated from the output back to the inputs to calculate partial derivatives.
teaches: A learner sees how a computational graph is used for a forward pass to compute a final function value and a backward pass to compute gradients via the chain rule.
benchmark_query: computational graph showing forward pass values and backward pass adjoints for variables w x y z a b u v f
source_title: The Chain Rule on Computational Graphs

title: Riemann Sum Convergence and Area Approximation
description: Three panels show how smaller slice widths (epsilon) create left-endpoint rectangles that more closely follow the black curve, resulting in a sum that approaches the true area value.
teaches: A learner sees how decreasing the width of rectangles in a Riemann sum leads to a better approximation of the true area under a curve.
benchmark_query: visualizing left-endpoint riemann sum convergence for f(x)=x/(1+x^2) as epsilon decreases from 0.5 to 0.05

title: Signed Area and Limits of Integration
description: A plot shows shaded lobes above and below the horizontal axis marked with plus and minus signs. Below, arrows demonstrate that integrating from a to b produces a sum, while integrating from b to a negates that sum.
teaches: A learner sees how definite integrals represent signed area, where regions below the x-axis are subtracted and reversing the limits of integration negates the total result.
benchmark_query: visual explanation of signed area in integration with plus and minus lobes and the formula for reversing integration limits from a to b

title: Geometric representation of the fundamental theorem of calculus
description: The area under a curve f from x1 to x2 is visualized as the total area from a base point a to x2 minus the area from a to x1. Three panels show shaded regions under the same bell-shaped curve to illustrate the subtraction of integrals.
teaches: A learner sees how a definite integral over an interval is geometrically equivalent to the difference between two areas starting from a common base point.
benchmark_query: visual proof that integral from x1 to x2 of f equals integral from a to x2 minus integral from a to x1 using shaded areas

title: Geometric intuition for Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
description: The area function F(x) is represented by a blue region under a curve f. When x is increased by epsilon, the additional area is approximately a rectangle with width epsilon and height f(x).
teaches: A learner sees how the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus relates the derivative of an area function to the value of the original function through a small rectangular approximation.
benchmark_query: geometric proof of fundamental theorem of calculus using area function F(x) and rectangle approximation epsilon times f(x)

title: Geometric Interpretation of Integral Substitution
description: The diagram compares two slices under a curve: one on the x-axis with width epsilon and height f(u(x)), and its transformed version with width epsilon times u'(x). This visualizes why the differential du is replaced by u'(x)dx during integration by substitution.
teaches: A learner sees how the substitution rule in calculus relates the width of a small area element to the derivative of the transformation function.
benchmark_query: visual explanation of integral substitution showing a sliver of width epsilon and epsilon u'(x) under a curve f(u(x))

title: Approximating Volume with Double Integrals
description: A 3D bar chart approximates the volume under the bell surface z = e^(-x^2-y^2). A specific slice of columns at a fixed x-coordinate is highlighted in orange to demonstrate the inner sum used in Fubini's theorem.
teaches: A learner sees how a double integral is approximated by summing the volumes of discrete rectangular columns under a 3D surface.
benchmark_query: 3D bar chart visualization of double integral for z = e^(-x^2-y^2) with highlighted column at fixed x representing an inner sum

title: Approximating Double Integrals via Column Sums

title: Soft-Thresholding and Proximal Operators

title: Convex and Nonconvex Sets

title: Geometric Definitions of Convexity
