title: Mixture-of-Experts Layer Architecture
description: An input passes through a gating network which determines the weights for specific experts. The selected expert outputs are multiplied by these weights and summed together to form the layer output.
teaches: A learner sees how a gating network selects and weights a subset of specialized expert modules within a neural network layer.
benchmark_query: diagram of MoE layer showing gating network G(x) selecting subset of experts with summation of weighted expert outputs
source_title: How to Train Really Large Models on Many GPUs?

title: Switch Transformer Mixture of Experts Architecture
description: The architecture replaces standard feed-forward layers with a switching layer where a router directs input tokens to one of several FFN experts. This process includes self-attention, residual connections, and normalization steps applied to token embeddings.
teaches: A learner sees how a Switch Transformer uses a router to select one specific feed-forward network expert for each token in a sequence.
benchmark_query: diagram of switch transformer switching FFN layer showing router selecting one expert FFN out of four with probability p
source_title: How to Train Really Large Models on Many GPUs?

title: Parallelism Strategies for Weights and Data
description: The diagram compares five parallelism configurations, showing how weight matrices and data tokens are distributed or replicated across a 4x4 grid of compute cores. Color coding distinguishes unique weights and unique data samples, revealing the trade-offs between data, model, and expert-based scaling.
teaches: A learner sees how model weights and data batches are partitioned across a grid of processor cores under different parallelism strategies including data, model, and expert parallelism.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing weight and data splitting for expert and model parallelism across a 4x4 grid of cores
source_title: How to Train Really Large Models on Many GPUs?

title: Mixed Precision Training Workflow
description: Master weights in F32 are converted to F16 for the forward and backward passes. Gradients calculated in F16 are then used to update the high-precision F32 master weights to prevent loss of precision.
teaches: A learner sees how mixed precision training utilizes FP16 for forward and backward passes while maintaining master weights in FP32 to ensure numerical stability during updates.
benchmark_query: diagram showing float2half conversion for FWD and BWD passes with F32 master weight update in neural networks
source_title: How to Train Really Large Models on Many GPUs?

title: Weight Gradient Distribution and FP16 Precision Limit
description: A histogram shows the distribution of weight gradient exponent values, with a red line indicating the cutoff where values smaller than 2^-24 become zero in FP16 representation. This demonstrates the risk of gradient vanishing when using lower-precision formats without scaling.
teaches: A learner sees how gradients with very small exponent values are clipped to zero when converting from full precision to FP16 mixed precision training.
benchmark_query: histogram of weight gradient exponent values showing the cutoff point where gradients become zero in FP16 mixed precision training
source_title: How to Train Really Large Models on Many GPUs?

title: Mean Teacher Semi-Supervised Learning Framework
description: The student model is updated via backpropagation from a combined loss, while the teacher model's weights are an exponential moving average (EMA) of the student's. Both models receive the same input with different noise, and a consistency loss (MSE) is calculated between their predictions alongside the student's classification loss.
teaches: A learner sees how a student model and a teacher model (updated via exponential moving average) collaborate to optimize a joint loss combining supervised cross-entropy and consistency-based mean squared error.
benchmark_query: diagram showing student f_theta and teacher f_theta' connected by EMA with loss L_s + mu(t)L_u in mean teacher framework
source_title: Learning with not Enough Data Part 1: Semi-Supervised Learning

title: Consistency Training for Semi-Supervised Learning
description: Labeled data passes through a model to calculate cross-entropy loss, while unlabeled data is processed both in its raw form and an augmented form to compute a Mean Squared Error (MSE) consistency loss. These two losses are combined using a time-dependent weighting factor to produce the final objective function.
teaches: A learner sees how a semi-supervised learning model combines supervised cross-entropy loss from labeled data with a consistency regularization loss (MSE) on original and augmented unlabeled data.
benchmark_query: diagram showing supervised cross entropy loss and MSE consistency loss between unlabeled sample u and augmented sample u-bar for semi-supervised learning
source_title: Learning with not Enough Data Part 1: Semi-Supervised Learning

title: Label Guessing with Augmentation Averaging and Sharpening
description: An unlabeled image is transformed into K augmentations which are each classified to produce individual probability distributions. These distributions are averaged together and then sharpened to create a high-confidence pseudo-label.
teaches: A learner sees the process of label guessing for unlabeled data by averaging model predictions across multiple augmentations and then sharpening the resulting distribution.
benchmark_query: diagram of K augmentations being classified averaged and sharpened for label guessing in semi-supervised learning
source_title: Learning with not Enough Data Part 1: Semi-Supervised Learning

title: FixMatch Semi-Supervised Learning Process
description: An unlabeled image is split into weak and strong augmentations; the model's high-confidence prediction for the weak augmentation becomes a pseudo-label used to supervise the prediction of the strong augmentation via cross-entropy loss H(p,q).
teaches: A learner sees how the FixMatch semi-supervised learning method uses consistency between weak and strong augmentations to generate and learn from pseudo-labels.
benchmark_query: diagram of FixMatch pipeline with unlabeled example split into weakly-augmented and strongly-augmented paths to produce pseudo-label and loss H(p,q)
source_title: Learning with not Enough Data Part 1: Semi-Supervised Learning

title: Semi-Supervised Learning with Pretraining and Distillation
description: Unlabeled data is used to pretrain a large CNN with a projection head before fine-tuning on a small labeled dataset. The resulting model is then used to label more unlabeled data for distilling into a task-specific CNN.
teaches: A learner sees how task-agnostic unsupervised pretraining on unlabeled data can be combined with supervised fine-tuning and task-specific distillation to create specialized models.
benchmark_query: three step process diagram showing task-agnostic big CNN unsupervised pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning and task-specific CNN distillation
source_title: Learning with not Enough Data Part 1: Semi-Supervised Learning

title: Multimodal Transformer Encoder-Decoder Architecture
description: Image patches pass through a convolutional stage while text tokens are embedded; both are combined with positional embeddings for the Transformer Encoder. The Transformer Decoder then uses this representation to autoregressively generate a textual description.
teaches: A learner sees how image patches and text tokens are separately embedded with positional encoding before being processed by a Transformer Encoder and Decoder to generate text.
benchmark_query: Architecture diagram showing image patches with Conv Stage and text tokens feeding into a Transformer Encoder for a Transformer Decoder text generation task.

title: ClipCap Image Captioning Architecture
description: An image is processed by a CLIP encoder to create an embedding, which is then transformed by a mapping network into a sequence of prefix embeddings. These prefixes are concatenated with caption tokens and fed into a GPT-2 model to generate a descriptive sentence.
teaches: A learner sees how a mapping network transforms a CLIP image embedding into prefix embeddings that guide a pre-trained GPT-2 model to generate a text caption.
benchmark_query: diagram of ClipCap architecture showing CLIP embedding transformation through a mapping network into prefix embeddings for GPT-2 caption generation

title: Flamingo Multi-modal Architecture with Gated Cross-Attention
description: The architecture connects a frozen vision encoder and language model using a Perceiver Resampler to extract visual features and Gated XATTN-DENSE layers for fusion. Interleaved text and images are processed so that the language model can generate text based on both visual and textual context.
teaches: A learner sees how Flamingo uses a Perceiver Resampler and Gated Cross-Attention to fuse interleaved visual and text data into a frozen language model.
benchmark_query: Flamingo architecture diagram showing perceiver resampler and gated cross-attention layers connecting frozen vision encoder and frozen LM blocks.

title: CoCa Contrastive Captioner Training Framework
description: The architecture processes image-text pairs through an image encoder and a unimodal text decoder. It calculates contrastive loss between global representations and captioning loss via a multimodal text decoder that uses cross-attention over image tokens.
teaches: A learner sees how the CoCa architecture combines a unimodal text decoder for contrastive loss and a multimodal text decoder for captioning loss using cross-attention.
benchmark_query: diagram of CoCa architecture showing unimodal text decoder for contrastive loss and multimodal text decoder with cross-attention for captioning loss

title: PICa Few-Shot VQA Architecture
description: Images are converted to text captions via an offline image-to-text model and formatted into an in-context learning prompt. This prompt, containing context and question-answer pairs, is passed to a frozen GPT-3 model to generate the final answer.
teaches: A learner sees how visual-language models can perform zero-shot or few-shot question answering by converting images into text captions and feeding them as context into a frozen large language model like GPT-3.
benchmark_query: diagram showing offline image-to-text model generating context for frozen gpt-3 in-context learning for n-shot vqa

title: Teacher-Student Knowledge Distillation Framework
description: A complex teacher model extracts knowledge which is then transferred to a significantly smaller student model. Both models process the same input data to align the student's outputs or internal representations with the teacher's.
teaches: A learner sees how a large, complex teacher model distills its knowledge into a smaller, simpler student model through a knowledge transfer process using a shared dataset.
benchmark_query: diagram showing teacher model distilling knowledge into a student model with shared data source and simplified neural network architecture

title: SmoothQuant activation outlier smoothing mechanism
description: The diagram compares original activations with large outliers to a smoothed version where the difficulty is migrated to the weight matrix. This process results in both weight and activation distributions having manageable quantization levels.
teaches: A learner sees how SmoothQuant migrates quantization difficulty from activations to weights by smoothing out outliers to achieve a balanced distribution.
benchmark_query: how smoothquant migrates difficulty from activations |X| with outliers to weights |W| to balance quantization levels

title: N:M Structured Sparsity Compression Mechanism
description: A sparse matrix W of size R x C is compressed into a smaller dense matrix of non-zero values and a 2-bit index matrix. The example shows a 2:4 pattern where every group of 4 columns is reduced to 2 non-zero entries, halving the storage width.
teaches: A learner sees how a sparse weight matrix with a 2:4 pattern can be compressed into a dense matrix of non-zero values and a corresponding metadata matrix of indices.
benchmark_query: diagram showing compression of sparse matrix W with R rows and C columns into non-zero data values and 2-bits indices for 2:4 sparsity

title: Standard MoE vs PR-MoE Architecture
description: Standard Mixture of Experts (MoE) maintains a constant number of experts across layers, while Pyramid Residual MoE (PR-MoE) increases the expert count in later layers. In PR-MoE, each token passes through both a fixed MLP block and a selected expert (E) from a layer-specific pool.
teaches: A learner sees how PR-MoE differs from standard MoE by using a varying number of experts per layer and adding a fixed MLP alongside chosen experts in a residual-like structure.
benchmark_query: Architecture comparison between standard MoE and PR-MoE showing expert layer L with more experts than layer 1 and fixed MLP residual connections.

title: Categorization of Efficient Transformer Models
description: A Venn diagram clusters models like Performer, Big Bird, and Reformer into groups based on architectural strategies: Low Rank/Kernels, Memory, Recurrence, Learnable Patterns, and Fixed/Factorized/Random Patterns.
teaches: A learner sees how various efficient transformer architectures are categorized and related based on their underlying mechanisms like low-rank kernels, memory, and sparsity patterns.
benchmark_query: Venn diagram comparing transformer models like Linformer, Longformer, Big Bird, and Reformer by memory, recurrence, and low rank kernel methods.

title: Transformer vs Transformer-XL Training Comparison
description: The left panel shows a standard Transformer processing independent segments, while the right panel shows Transformer-XL using a cache of fixed hidden states from a previous segment to inform the new segment's calculations.
teaches: A learner sees how Transformer-XL reuses hidden states from previous segments as memory to capture longer-range dependencies compared to the vanilla Transformer.
benchmark_query: comparison of vanilla transformer and transformer-xl training with segment reuse and fixed no-gradient cached hidden states x1 through x12

title: Compressive Transformer Memory Mechanism
description: The diagram illustrates a sequence of activations where recent tokens are kept in active memory, while older blocks are processed by a compression function f_c to be stored in a dense compressed memory buffer.
teaches: A learner sees how older memory activations are compressed into a more compact form to extend the context window of a sequence model over time.
benchmark_query: compressive transformer diagram showing f_c(1) f_c(2) f_c(3) functions mapping memory blocks to compressed memory slots over time t

title: ALiBi Attention with Positional Bias
description: The attention mechanism is modified by adding a triangular matrix of negative distance penalties to the standard query-key dot products. This total score is scaled by a head-specific factor m to bias the model toward more recent tokens.
teaches: A learner sees how positional bias is added to query-key attention scores by summing a dot-product matrix with a distance-based penalty matrix scaled by a factor m.
benchmark_query: ALiBi attention diagram showing qk dot product matrix addition with a matrix of negative integers 0 to -4 scaled by m

title: Universal Transformer Recurrent Structure
description: Hidden states for each position pass through a shared self-attention layer and a transition function at each time step. The output states serve as the input for the next time step, refining representations over time while maintaining weight sharing.
teaches: A learner sees how a Universal Transformer applies self-attention and transition functions recurrently across multiple time steps while tying parameters across positions.
benchmark_query: diagram of universal transformer refining hidden states h_m^t through self-attention and transition functions across time steps with tied parameters

title: Local 1D vs 2D Attention in Images
description: The diagram compares 1D and 2D attention windows where a specific query pixel 'q' in a black box attends to a surrounding memory block outlined in cyan. It illustrates how local context windows are defined for autoregressive image generation.
teaches: A learner sees how local 1D and 2D attention mechanisms restrict the receptive field of a pixel query within an image to specific memory blocks.
benchmark_query: diagram of local 1D attention vs local 2D attention memory blocks for a pixel q in a query block

title: Comparison of Sparse Attention Patterns
description: These attention matrices compare three efficient transformer variants. They visualize how tokens attend to each other using local sliding windows, global memory tokens, strided patterns, and random sampling.
teaches: A learner sees how ETC, Longformer, and Big Bird models utilize different combinations of local, global, strided, and random attention to reduce the computational complexity of the standard self-attention mechanism.
benchmark_query: Compare attention patterns for ETC, Longformer and Big Bird showing local, global, strided and random attention blocks with window size 2w+1.

title: LSH Attention Processing Steps
description: The diagram illustrates the pipeline of LSH attention, where sequence elements are first bucketed by color, sorted to bring similar elements together, and then divided into chunks. Attention is then restricted to elements within the same bucket across current and previous chunks to maintain efficiency.
teaches: A learner sees how Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) attention reduces complexity by bucketing, sorting, and chunking queries and keys to allow for parallelized, localized attention.
benchmark_query: diagram showing sequence of queries and keys undergoing LSH bucketing, sorting by bucket, and chunking for parallelized attention within same bucket

title: Comparison of TrXL, TrXL-I, and GTrXL Architectures
description: Three diagrams contrast standard Transformer-XL blocks with variants that use pre-activation layer normalization and gating mechanisms. Arrows show the flow from Multi-Head Attention through Position-Wise MLPs, highlighting where Gating Layers replace simple addition.
teaches: A learner sees how the Gated Transformer-XL (GTrXL) modifies the standard Transformer-XL by reordering layer normalization and introducing gating layers into the residual connections.
benchmark_query: comparison diagram of TrXL vs TrXL-I vs GTrXL architectures showing gating layer and layer-norm placement

title: Tree of Thoughts Reasoning Framework
description: A hierarchical tree structure shows an input branching into multiple potential reasoning steps called 'thoughts'. Some paths are discarded (pink) while others are pursued (green) to eventually converge on a final output.
teaches: A learner sees how the Tree of Thoughts (ToT) framework explores multiple reasoning paths by branching out from an initial input through intermediate 'thoughts' to reach an optimal output.
benchmark_query: diagram of tree of thoughts ToT branching process with green successful thought paths and pink discarded reasoning steps

title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agent Architecture
description: An agent acts as a central hub connecting planning strategies like chain of thought to tools, memory systems, and resulting actions. It breaks down complex tasks using subgoal decomposition and self-critics while maintaining both short-term and long-term memory.
teaches: A learner sees the core architecture of an LLM-powered agent system, connecting the central agent brain to its memory, planning capabilities, tools, and actions.
benchmark_query: architecture diagram of an LLM agent showing the relationship between planning, memory, tools, and action components like chain of thought and reflection

title: The Reflexion Framework for LLM Agents
description: The diagram illustrates a feedback loop where an agent's actions, environment observations, and rewards are processed by a heuristic. This heuristic feeds into an LLM-based reflection module that provides corrective feedback back into the initial query prompt to improve subsequent performance.
teaches: A learner sees how the Reflexion framework augments the standard ReAct loop by passing action history and rewards through a heuristic to generate self-reflections that influence future queries.
benchmark_query: diagram of reflexion framework showing interaction between ReAct loop and Reflect loop with heuristic h and reflection LLM feeding back to query

title: Algorithm Distillation via Causal Transformers
description: Data generation collects histories of observations, actions, and rewards across multiple tasks to capture learning progress. These histories are fed into a causal transformer that learns to predict the next action given the prior history and current observation.
teaches: A learner sees how reinforcement learning histories from multiple tasks are used as training data for a causal transformer to predict actions based on across-episodic contexts.
benchmark_query: diagram showing how algorithm distillation uses RL algorithm learning histories h_T to train a causal transformer for action prediction P_theta(a_t|h_t-1, o_t)

title: SelfCheckGPT Factuality Evaluation Workflow
description: An LLM generates a target passage and several independent samples on the same topic. The system then prompts the LLM to check if each sentence in the target passage is supported by the generated samples, producing a final consistency score.
teaches: A learner sees how the SelfCheckGPT method evaluates the factuality of an LLM-generated passage by comparing individual sentences against multiple stochastic samples from the same model.
benchmark_query: SelfCheckGPT diagram showing how stochastically-generated responses sample1 to sampleN are used to evaluate an LLM's passage at sentence-level with yes/no support answers.

title: Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) Process
description: The diagram illustrates how a model generates a baseline response, creates verification questions to check its own claims, executes those verifications, and synthesizes a final corrected response.
teaches: A learner sees the four steps of the Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) method for correcting model hallucinations.
benchmark_query: 4-step chain-of-verification CoVe process diagram with baseline response plan verifications execute verifications and final verified response

title: Direct Generation vs RAG vs RECITE
description: The diagram compares three LLM architectures: direct answering from memory, retrieval-based answering using external snippets, and recitation-based answering where the model generates its own supporting context before the answer.
teaches: A learner sees how Direct Generation, Retrieval-augmented Generation (RAG), and Recitation-augmented Generation differ in their information flow between prompt input and final model output.
benchmark_query: comparison of direct generation vs retrieval-augmented generation vs recitation-augmented generation showing prompt input and recitation output blocks

title: RAG pipeline with Reward Model reranking
description: The process starts with a question and a Google search for top-K documents, which are fed into a generator. The generator produces multiple samples (xN) that are scored by a reward model to select the best sample with citations for UI rendering.
teaches: A learner sees how a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline uses search results to generate multiple samples which are then reranked by a reward model to produce a final attributed claim.
benchmark_query: diagram of question answering flow with Google Search top-K documents feeding a generator and reward model scoring multiple samples for attribution

title: Parallel Sampling vs Sequential Revision
description: The diagram compares two LLM strategies: parallel sampling branches out from a single prompt to multiple candidates, while sequential revision shows a single path of iterative edits leading to a final result.
teaches: A learner sees the difference between generating multiple independent outputs simultaneously to find a correct one versus iteratively refining a single output until it is correct.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing parallel sampling branching from one prompt versus sequential revision chain with checkmarks and x marks

title: Top-k Branching for Chain of Thought Reasoning
description: The diagram shows a language model processing a math word problem and generating five candidate tokens at 'Decoding step 0'. Each branch is followed by greedy decoding, where branches starting with 'I' or 'You' lead to successful multi-step reasoning, while others fail.
teaches: A learner sees how branching at the first decoding step by selecting top-k candidates can reveal latent chain-of-thought reasoning paths that lead to correct answers.
benchmark_query: diagram showing how branching at decoding step 0 with top-k candidates leads to chain of thought reasoning paths for a math problem

title: Chain of Thought Perturbation Methods
description: Five parallel scenarios compare a standard chain-of-thought response to variations including early answering, adding mistakes, paraphrasing, and filler tokens. Each path shows an initial assistant response followed by a user prompt for the final answer and the resulting model output.
teaches: A learner sees how different perturbations to chain-of-thought reasoning, such as adding mistakes or using filler tokens, impact a model's final answer consistency.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing chain of thought faithfulness using early answering adding mistakes paraphrasing and filler tokens for the factorial of 5

title: Pause Tokens for Computational Delay
description: Standard inference is compared to pause-inference where dummy tokens are inserted into the input sequence. These tokens trigger additional hidden layer computations while their immediate outputs are ignored, effectively giving the model more time to 'think' before producing the next real token.
teaches: A learner sees how injecting special pause tokens into an input sequence allows a transformer model to perform additional computational layers before generating a target output.
benchmark_query: diagram comparing standard inference vs pause-inference with ignore output tokens and hidden layer depth for mathematical reasoning tasks

title: Quiet-STaR Token-Level Reasoning Process
description: The model generates a sequence of hidden thought tokens between original text tokens to predict the next character. Correct predictions from these sampled thoughts lead to rewards and learning, while incorrect ones are discarded.
teaches: A learner sees how a language model uses intermediate 'thought' tokens to improve next-token prediction, rewarding thoughts that help accuracy and discarding those that harm it.
benchmark_query: diagram showing Quiet-STaR process of generating Sampled Thoughts between original text tokens to improve next-token prediction with reward and discard paths
